nodes.title: Stateless Request Handling
nodes.summary: Request handling lets any replica serve any request without relying on replica-local sessions, uploads, or durable work, while mutable state lives in shared durable services. This preserves state across load-balancer rebalancing and replica restarts.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect handlers for process globals, in-memory session maps, local upload paths, and fire-and-forget durable work; route two sequential requests to different replicas and verify session, upload, and job state remain available after restarting the first replica.

nodes.title: Replica-Safe Coordination
nodes.summary: Replica-safe coordination puts singleton ownership and mutual exclusion in a shared mechanism that survives process restarts and arbitrates concurrent replicas. Leases, fencing, and expiration prevent duplicate singleton work and enable takeover after failure.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect singleton jobs and lock call graphs for process-local flags; run two replicas against the same schedule and kill the lease holder, verifying one owner at a time and takeover after expiry without concurrent side effects.

nodes.title: Ephemeral Local Disk
nodes.summary: Local disk is limited to disposable scratch data, while durable uploads, exports, and artifacts use shared storage with ownership, retention, and access controls. This keeps files available through restart, rescheduling, and load balancing.
nodes.probe: Scan application code and deployment manifests for writes outside the allowlisted temporary directory, then fail if upload, export, or artifact paths target replica-local storage; restart a replica mid-transfer and verify the shared object remains retrievable.

nodes.title: Graceful Drain on Scale Down
nodes.summary: Scale-down drain removes a replica from readiness, stops admission of new work, honors SIGTERM, and completes or safely cancels in-flight work within a bounded grace period. Correct deregistration and keep-alive behavior prevent resets, dropped work, and retry storms.
nodes.probe: Parse lifecycle and readiness settings, send SIGTERM to a running replica under active requests, and assert readiness fails before exit, new requests stop, and existing requests complete or are safely canceled without dropped or duplicated completions.

nodes.title: Retry-Safe Mutations
nodes.summary: Retry-safe mutations bind retries to an idempotency key or durable deduplication record whose scope, fingerprint, and retention cover every retry path. Replays return the original result without repeating the committed side effect.
nodes.probe: Submit the same mutation concurrently and after a forced response timeout with one idempotency key, then assert one durable side effect and equivalent replay responses; submit the same key with a changed payload and assert a deterministic conflict.

nodes.title: Connection Pool Budget
nodes.summary: A connection-pool budget reserves database connections across maximum replicas and all non-application consumers, keeping pool limits below the database limit after migrations, operators, failover, and safety reserve. This prevents horizontal rollout and failover connection exhaustion.
nodes.probe: Parse deployment replica maximum, per-process pool maximum, pooler limits, and database `max_connections`, then assert the inequality including documented reserve; exercise max replicas and verify no connection refusals.

nodes.title: Pool Timeouts and Leak Detection
nodes.summary: Pool safety uses finite acquisition, connect, idle, lifetime, and query deadlines plus telemetry for waiting, in-use, idle, and leaked checkouts. A dependency stall must release capacity rather than pinning every worker.
nodes.probe: Parse timeout settings and run a dependency-stall test, asserting bounded request time, pool-wait telemetry, checkout release after cancellation, and recovery when the dependency returns.

nodes.title: Connection Pooler Boundary
nodes.summary: A pooler boundary multiplexes application clients onto controlled database backends when replica fan-out would otherwise exceed limits. Transaction pooling is safe only when session state is not required between transactions.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect pooler mode and application session-state usage, then run representative transactions through failover and concurrent replicas, verifying prepared statements, tenant context, locks, and notifications retain their documented semantics.

nodes.title: Access Path Indexes
nodes.summary: Access-path indexes are selected from measured production query predicates, joins, and ordering to provide selective paths for high-volume shapes at acceptable write and storage cost. This prevents data growth from turning lookups and joins into scans.
nodes.probe: Run representative queries with `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)` against production-shaped cardinalities and fail when a required selective access path is absent or estimated work exceeds its budget.

nodes.title: Composite Index Order
nodes.summary: Composite-index order places equality predicates first, then useful range and ordering columns, with a unique tie-breaker for stable pagination boundaries. Validating order against real query shapes avoids unusable or expensive indexes.
nodes.probe: Execute each high-volume query shape with `EXPLAIN` and assert the plan uses the intended equality prefix, range condition, and ordering without a large residual sort or scan.

nodes.title: Index Write Amplification
nodes.summary: Index-write review measures read benefit against insert/update work, storage, cache pressure, replication, and backup volume. Unused or redundant indexes are removed only after confirming important query coverage remains.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect index-usage history, write amplification, storage/replication cost, and query coverage evidence; verify proposed drops account for low-frequency critical paths and have a rollback window.

nodes.title: Plan Regression Gates
nodes.summary: A plan-regression gate versions representative query plans and compares estimated rows, actual rows, buffers, and duration across schema, statistics, and engine changes. It stops materially more expensive critical queries before release.
nodes.probe: Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON)` on fixed production-shaped fixtures before and after a change and fail on configured plan-node, row-estimate, buffer, or latency regressions.

nodes.title: N Plus One Query Budget
nodes.summary: An N+1 query budget limits database round trips per request independently of returned collection size, with instrumentation exposing query counts and database spans. Bounded batches or joins prevent collection growth from saturating the database.
nodes.probe: Exercise each collection endpoint with fixtures containing 1, 10, and 100 related records and fail if database-query count grows linearly with collection size.

nodes.title: Endpoint Latency and Query Budget
nodes.summary: A per-endpoint budget assigns p95 and p99 end-to-end latency limits and allocates portions to application, database, and downstream dependencies. Explicit budgets tie tail behavior to user experience, traffic, and the SLO rather than informal averages.
nodes.probe: Ask: “Which endpoint classes must meet which p95/p99 end-to-end, database, and dependency budgets over what measurement window?” Present options: (A) document route-specific values and owners now, (B) adopt a proposed baseline and review after one traffic window, or (C) explicitly defer the SLO with a named risk owner and deadline.

nodes.title: Bounded Query Work
nodes.summary: Bounded query work caps rows, sort and join effort, execution time, and memory for every externally influenced query across API, ORM, database, and governance layers. These bounds prevent one request from monopolizing shared database capacity.
nodes.probe: Lint query construction for missing limits or timeouts, then run worst-case cardinality fixtures with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and assert bounded rows, memory, and duration.

nodes.title: Keyset Pagination
nodes.summary: Keyset pagination uses an opaque cursor over a stable, unique, indexed ordering instead of an ever-growing OFFSET. It keeps work predictable and defines behavior when rows change between pages.
nodes.probe: Request a deep page while capturing the query plan and assert it uses a cursor range predicate on the ordering index, not a growing OFFSET scan; tamper with the cursor and assert a documented error.

nodes.title: Bounded Page Contract
nodes.summary: A bounded page contract enforces server-side size limits, deterministic tie-broken ordering, allowed fields, and a valid next-cursor representation. Invalid or excessive requests fail predictably rather than allocating unbounded query and response work.
nodes.probe: Call the list endpoint with zero, negative, maximum-plus-one, and very large page sizes and assert bounded responses, deterministic ordering, and a valid next-cursor or documented error.

nodes.title: Cache Control Contract
nodes.summary: Cache-control explicitly classifies responses as public, private, or non-cacheable and assigns deliberate freshness and revalidation semantics. The policy protects sensitive data in shared caches while reducing safe origin work.
nodes.probe: Fetch representative public, authenticated, mutable, and error responses with `curl -I` and assert expected `Cache-Control`, freshness, and `no-store` or `private` directives.

nodes.title: Validators and Revalidation
nodes.summary: Validators let clients and caches prove a representation is current without downloading its body again, using correctly scoped ETags or Last-Modified values and 304 responses. This reduces bandwidth and origin serialization work without serving stale content.
nodes.probe: Fetch a cacheable response, replay it with `If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since`, and assert a correct 304 with no response body and unchanged validator semantics; alter the resource and assert a full response with a new validator.

nodes.title: Cache Key Variation
nodes.summary: Cache-key variation includes every dimension that changes a representation, including encoding, locale, tenant, authorization, and content negotiation. Correct variation prevents cross-tenant or wrong-format responses while preserving safe cache hits.
nodes.probe: Request the same URL across each supported encoding, locale, tenant, and authentication state and assert distinct authorized bodies or an explicit non-shared-cache policy.

nodes.title: Immutable Versioned Assets
nodes.summary: Immutable asset delivery uses content-derived filenames and long-lived immutable caching while keeping the entry manifest short-lived and revalidatable. New URLs for changed bytes prevent stale JavaScript and CSS after deployment.
nodes.probe: Parse the build manifest for content hashes and fetch hashed and unhashed assets, asserting hashed responses have a long `max-age` with `immutable` and the manifest has a short revalidation policy.

nodes.title: App Cache Stampede Control
nodes.summary: Stampede control coordinates concurrent cache misses so one request refreshes a hot key while bounded waiters reuse its result or a safe stale value. TTL jitter, leases, and negative caching prevent synchronized expiry from flooding the origin.
nodes.probe: Expire one hot key and issue concurrent misses while counting origin calls, then assert one refresh, bounded waiters, and explicit stale or error behavior on refresh failure.

nodes.title: Cache Invalidation Ownership
nodes.summary: Every mutable cached object has an owner and tested invalidation or versioning mechanism, with TTL as a bounded safety net. Ownership defines ordering, scope, recovery, and acceptable staleness so freshness cannot silently diverge.
nodes.probe: Ask: “For each mutable cache, who owns freshness and what happens when invalidation delivery fails?” Present options: (A) event/version-based invalidation with bounded TTL, (B) synchronous purge on every mutation, or (C) explicitly accept bounded stale data with owner, TTL, and incident procedure.

nodes.title: Cache Hit Observability
nodes.summary: Cache observability measures hit, miss, age, eviction, stale-serve, origin-fallback, and cache-latency behavior by region and key class. Correlating cache state with origin load exposes capacity failures hidden by nominal cache health.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect metric definitions, bounded labels, dashboards, and alerts; expire a hot key and induce cache/origin failure to verify hit/miss, stale, fallback, latency, and origin-load signals distinguish each state.

nodes.title: CDN Origin Offload
nodes.summary: CDN origin offload routes static and safely cacheable public responses through edge caches with deliberate cache, compression, and origin-shield policies. It reduces origin requests while preserving correctness for dynamic and private traffic.
nodes.probe: Fetch representative objects through the public CDN URL and assert cache status or Age headers, expected TTL and encoding, and measurable reduction in origin requests during repeated loads.

nodes.title: Load Balancer Affinity Policy
nodes.summary: Load-balancer affinity is disabled unless a documented stateful requirement justifies it, and any stickiness specifies key, lifetime, rebalance behavior, and fallback. This keeps load distributable and makes replica loss survivable.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect balancer policy, affinity key/lifetime, state dependencies, removal behavior, and per-replica distribution under scale-out and failure; verify a client can continue on another replica when its target disappears.

nodes.title: Hash Routing Stability
nodes.summary: Consistent hash routing maps an explicit stable key to nodes while bounding remapping when membership changes. Missing-key, overloaded-node, and unavailable-node fallbacks keep requests routable rather than treating assignment as guaranteed capacity.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect hash key choice, ring/weight settings, node-change algorithm, health fallback, and skew metrics; add/remove a node and verify remapping stays within the stated bound while requests remain routable.

nodes.title: Health Check and Drain
nodes.summary: Health-aware routing separates process liveness from dependency-aware readiness and combines active checks, outlier removal, and connection draining. An overloaded or dependency-isolated replica is withdrawn while healthy replicas serve and existing work drains safely.
nodes.probe: Make a replica fail each critical dependency and enter drain mode, then assert the balancer stops new requests while healthy replicas continue serving and existing connections finish.

nodes.title: Autoscale on Work Signals
nodes.summary: Autoscaling follows the resource or work signal that limits throughput, such as queue depth, active concurrency, request rate, or tail latency, alongside CPU when useful. This avoids CPU-only decisions that miss I/O overload or add replicas beyond dependency capacity.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the selected signals, target derivation, stabilization behavior, and missing-data policy; apply CPU-light I/O load and CPU-heavy load separately and verify each scales according to the actual bottleneck.

nodes.title: Autoscale Stability Guards
nodes.summary: Autoscaler stability guards bound capacity changes and account for startup, warm-up, dependency saturation, and metric lag. Minimum and maximum replicas, stabilization windows, cooldowns, and rate limits prevent oscillation and cold-start amplification.
nodes.probe: Parse autoscaler policy and run a step-load and step-down test, asserting bounded scale rate, no oscillation, sufficient warm capacity, and convergence after load changes.

nodes.title: Bounded Concurrency Backpressure
nodes.summary: Backpressure bounds admitted work at request, queue, body-size, and downstream-concurrency layers and returns an explicit overload outcome when capacity is exhausted. It preserves recovery capacity instead of allowing queues and memory to grow without limit.
nodes.probe: Apply load beyond configured capacity and assert in-flight work and memory remain bounded while excess requests receive documented 429, 503, or queue responses; verify recovery after load stops.

nodes.title: Capacity Headroom Model
nodes.summary: A capacity model relates peak and burst workload to per-replica throughput, dependency limits, failure scenarios, scaling lag, and explicit headroom. Its measured assumptions and review triggers prevent average-throughput planning from missing saturation and failover conditions.
nodes.probe: Ask: “What peak/burst demand, failure tolerance, per-replica capacity, dependency ceiling, scaling lag, and headroom should capacity guarantee?” Present options: (A) N+1 capacity at documented peak, (B) N+2 or regional-failure capacity, (C) lower headroom with explicit load shedding and risk acceptance; record numeric thresholds and owner.

nodes.title: Representative Load and Soak Tests
nodes.summary: Representative performance testing exercises ramp, peak, spike, soak, and dependency-failure behavior with production-shaped data, request mix, concurrency, and cache state. Measuring degradation and recovery exposes leaks, queue buildup, and warm-up effects that short happy-path tests miss.
nodes.probe: Parse load-test scenarios for ramp, steady, spike, soak, data-shape, and failure phases, execute them in an isolated environment, and record latency, errors, throughput, saturation, queue age, memory, and recovery against documented thresholds.

nodes.title: Performance Regression Gate
nodes.summary: A performance gate compares a release candidate with a versioned baseline on p50, p95, p99, errors, throughput, and resource per request under the same workload. Agreed thresholds and measurement variance prevent functional success from hiding costly regressions.
nodes.probe: Run the fixed benchmark workload for baseline and candidate, calculate confidence-bounded metric deltas, and fail the release when configured latency, throughput, error, or resource thresholds regress.

nodes.title: JavaScript and CSS Budget
nodes.summary: Frontend asset budgets cap compressed transfer, parse, and execution cost per route and entrypoint, with code splitting and dependency checks. This prevents users from downloading and executing features unrelated to the requested route.
nodes.probe: Build the application, measure raw and Brotli or gzip sizes per entry and route chunk, and fail when transfer or execution budgets are exceeded; verify a route does not eagerly load unrelated chunks.

nodes.title: Compression Content Encoding
nodes.summary: Content encoding negotiates Brotli or gzip once for compressible representations and advertises the selected encoding and variation to intermediaries. Correct negotiation avoids wasted bandwidth, double compression, and cache corruption.
nodes.probe: Request representative text assets with and without `Accept-Encoding` using `curl`, then assert negotiated encoding, correct `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, valid decompression, and no duplicate encoding.

nodes.title: Responsive Image Delivery
nodes.summary: Responsive image delivery selects appropriately sized modern formats while declaring dimensions, deferring below-the-fold work, and enforcing quality and byte limits. This controls transfer, decode, and layout cost on constrained clients.
nodes.probe: Parse rendered image markup and the asset manifest, asserting responsive source variants, dimensions, modern formats, below-fold lazy loading, and per-image byte limits.

nodes.title: Hot Partition Safe Keys
nodes.summary: A hot-partition-safe key distributes traffic and storage across shards with sufficient cardinality and avoids monotonic or single-dominant values as the sole partition key. Evaluating access patterns and skew prevents one shard throttling while aggregate capacity remains unused.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect key cardinality, write/read distribution, dominant-tenant behavior, and growth projections; replay production-shaped traffic and verify no partition approaches its throughput or size limit while aggregate capacity remains available.

nodes.title: Bucketed Partitions and Rebalance
nodes.summary: Bucketed partitioning salts unavoidable hot logical keys with bounded fan-out and provides an online repartitioning path before growth makes migration urgent. Shared bucket discovery and migration controls prevent lost, duplicated, or unboundedly fanned-out reads.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect bucket count, fan-out/read budget, assignment versioning, migration tooling, reconciliation, rollback, and trigger thresholds; load a dominant tenant/time window and verify online redistribution without lost or duplicated records.
